::: {.block title="Introduction"}
Resolving the spatiotemporal variability of chlorophyll *a* (Chl *a*) throughout the euphotic zone, including subsurface chlorophyll maxima, helps characterize phytoplankton distributions and constrain estimates of depth-integrated primary production. Previous research (Sauzède et al., 2016, 2024) has established that satellite remote-sensing reflectance at multiple bands can be used to infer subsurface Chl *a* concentration and locations of subsurface chlorophyll peaks in the open ocean. In this pilot study, we test whether hyperspectral PACE improves Chl *a* profile estimates relative to multispectral observations and whether the approach transfers to coastal waters.

**Relation to existing approaches.** The Copernicus Marine 3D chlorophyll product (SOCA2024; Sauzède et al.) predicts 4D Chl *a*
profiles with neural networks trained on BGC-Argo, from 5-band $R_{rs}$ plus physical
fields. It is weekly at 0.25°, covers only water deeper than 1000 m, and currently ends in
December 2023. Our model (CHLA-Z) is very similar and is used to explore whether daily hyperspectral (172 $R_{rs}$ bands) improves 4D Chl *a* estimation and tests prediction in coastal (slope and shelf) regions.

